title: Unending Project of Building Racial Harmony in Singapore
what_it_is: Unending Project of Building Racial Harmony in Singapore

sections.label: Racial harmony as ongoing project
sections.summary: Racial harmony is an aspiration and a project that must be worked towards consistently and unendingly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Racial harmony is an aspiration and a project that we must consistently and unendingly work towards.

sections.label: Young Sikh Association responds to post
sections.summary: The Young Sikh Association reached out to influencer Ms Sheena Phua after her Instagram post called Sikh turbans obstructions, turning a divisive post positive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: An example is the Young Sikh Association, or the YSA, reaching out to influencer Ms Sheena Phua after she made an Instagram post describing Sikh turbans as "obstructions" obstructing her view of the Singapore Grand Prix race.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The YSA's actions helped turn a divisive post into something positive for all Singaporeans.

sections.label: Leaders and race conversations
sections.summary: The speaker agrees with Raeesah Khan on leaders starting difficult conversations, and was heartened by Teo and Pritam Singh's commitment not to politicise race issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I agree with fellow Member Raeesah Khan that, and I quote, "as leaders, we have the power to start difficult conversations and that it is vital to frame these conversations in a considerate and accountable manner".

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I was also heartened today to see that both Senior Minister Teo and the hon Leader of the Opposition Mr Pritam Singh affirmed their commitment not to politicise race issues.

sections.label: Ms Bagharib's standee complaint
sections.summary: The speaker first thought Ms Bagharib's Instagram post about PA using her photo as a standee without consent was a genuine complaint rooted in intellectual property rights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When I first saw Ms Bagharib's Instagram post about PA using her photo as a standee without her consent, I thought that she had a genuine and legitimate complaint primarily rooted in intellectual property rights.

sections.label: PA disengagement decision
sections.summary: If this was Ms Bagharib's intention, the speaker thinks the PA probably made the correct decision to disengage at that point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If indeed this was Ms Bagharib's intention, then I think that the PA probably made the correct decision to disengage at that point.

sections.label: SAP schools' contemporary purpose
sections.summary: SAP schools originate in old Chinese-education schools but now aim to build Singaporeans versed in Chinese culture and language to engage China.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SAP schools have origins in the Chinese-education schools of old but their contemporary purpose is to build a group of Singaporeans well versed in Chinese culture and language to engage China, the world's second superpower and second largest economy.

sections.label: Purpose of SAP schools
sections.summary: The speaker says SAP schools have a practical and pragmatic purpose, and doubts Malay or Tamil SAP schools would fulfil the same purposes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There is therefore a practical and pragmatic purpose to the SAP schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, let us take a step back and ask ourselves whether Malay SAP schools or Tamil SAP schools would fulfill the same purposes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My view is that it would be unlikely.

sections.label: SAP schools conversational Malay programmes
sections.summary: Minister Lawrence Wong updated the House that all SAP schools will eventually offer conversational Malay programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Last year, Minister Lawrence Wong updated the House that all SAP schools will eventually offer conversational Malay programmes.

sections.label: GRC system minority representation
sections.summary: The speaker's view is that the GRC system has worked well in ensuring minority representation and renewal of minority candidates in elections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My view is that the GRC system has worked well in ensuring minority representation and the renewal of minority candidates in the elections.

sections.label: GRC system removes post-election claims
sections.summary: The GRC system removes the possibility of this being claimed post-elections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The GRC system removes the possibility of this being claimed post-elections.

sections.label: Survey on Prime Minister's race
sections.summary: The 2016 CNA-IPS Survey showed Singaporeans preferred a Prime Minister of the same race but over 50% accepted one of another race.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In fact, Sir, if we look at the 2016 CNA-IPS Survey, which showed that while Singaporeans preferred a Prime Minister of the same race, the same survey also showed that Singaporeans were accepting – all above 50% – of a Prime Minister of another race.

sections.label: Racism frequency and racial harmony work
sections.summary: The speaker cites surveys on racism and says work remains to engage, communicate, calibrate and strengthen racial harmony.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And I think, Sir, when Minister Shanmugam is not so sure about something, we should at least be a little concerned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And in fact, the recent IPS World Value Survey showed that although Singapore has the second lowest proportion of respondents perceiving racism as occurring frequently, that the frequency of racist behaviour has been going up since 2012.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So we still have work to do, to engage, to communicate, to calibrate and to strengthen our racial harmony.

sections.label: Minority representation and integration safeguards
sections.summary: The electoral system, housing policies and Presidential Council on Minority Rights guarantee minority representation and integrated neighbourhoods.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Our electoral system guarantees minority representation in Parliament; and in each political party who wishes to represent the interests of Singaporeans and no political party can prevail by narrowly appealing to one narrow racial or religious segment of society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Our housing policies, as you have heard, ensure that we have racially integrated neighbourhoods and not segregated ethnic enclaves.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Our Presidential Council on Minority Rights has the power to reject laws passed by Parliament that infringes on the rights of any minority population.

sections.label: Ministry to study proposals
sections.summary: The Ministry, with other Ministries, will study them carefully.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: My Ministry, together with other Ministries, will study them carefully.

sections.label: Enlarging common spaces
sections.summary: Enlarging common spaces addresses the need to ensure SAP school students do not become insular.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Second, enlarging our common spaces, something which Mr Thomas spoke at some length about, highlighting the need to ensure, in particular, that students from SAP schools do not turn into an insular group.

sections.label: SG Cares and Alliances for Action
sections.summary: SG Cares Volunteer Centres coordinate volunteers and resources, and 25 Alliances for Action tackle complex issues across sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: At the neighbourhood-level, we have appointed SG Cares Volunteer Centres to coordinate volunteers and resources to bring more local stakeholders working side by side on a daily basis to create a larger positive social impact, regardless of race or religion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In the spirit of Singapore Together, we have embarked on 25 Alliances for Action (AfAs), which are action-oriented across different sector collaborations to tackle complex issues.

sections.label: MCCY social media harmony collaboration
sections.summary: MCCY collaborates with technology companies to help religious and community organisations produce positive social media content on racial and religious harmony.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: They also play a part in rallying Singaporeans to stand against divisive rhetoric, a lot of which also appears online.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: That is why MCCY is collaborating with technology companies, as I outlined earlier this afternoon, to support religious, interfaith and community organisations’ efforts to produce meaningful social media content, positive social media content on racial and religious harmony.

sections.label: Guarantee of racial equality and harmony
sections.summary: Singapore has a guarantee of equality for all races and racial harmony from a system set up by earlier leaders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It is a constant work in progress and we must take nothing for granted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: But we are also different from so many others in the world with what we already have: we have a guarantee of equality for all races; a racial diversity and harmony which has benefited from a system earlier generations of our leaders have set up, with wisdom and with foresight precisely to ensure that we do not fall into the difficulties that other racially diverse communities might have, with social mixing, integration, harmony.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: But we make a conscious choice that this is what our country will stand for on the very day of our Independence and have worked hard at it ever since.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: So, Sir, let us not throw out what has worked well for us over the decades, a system which structurally delivers integration outcomes to foster better multi-racial and multi-religious relations.
